Ha... if the price is that low, shouldn't the quality and taste follow? I'm a little sick of the taste with that kind of quality, but it has a unique meaty smell... 48,000 won? Really... Gimbap Heaven's earthen pot bulgogi is also 9,000 won per person, and it's much more delicious. It doesn't even include steamed rice... Ha... Why is the Pyongyang naengmyeon noodles so spicy... Why is the meat that goes on top so tough? That's one thing... I felt so bad that I trusted the location and the old Pyongyang Naengmyeon restaurant without looking at the reviews. Whenever I have free time for a precious meal, I find and eat my favorite Pyongyang cold noodles at a place I go to...ㅠㅠ It's so unfair.
Isn’t it embarrassing? There will be a lot of tourists there too..
The 100-year store is a mess. Go to Japan, go to the local izakaya, and tell them. Tsk tsk.
And at a store like that, shouldn’t they use Chinese kimchi? Is it good to use Kimbap Heaven kimchi? Seriously, even as I keep writing this review, I'm still thinking about it and getting angry.
Wow, look for reviews. Is there anything that uses this much? A store of that level has the same level of quality and service mindset. The taste is the same, so don't mistake yourself for being lucky enough to survive.

I went to the Seongsura Euljiro branch, a restaurant near Euljiro 3-ga Station. It is close to Euljiro 3-ga Station on subway lines 2 and 3. It is located in Euljiro Golbaengi Alley. It's on the 2nd floor of the building. Go up the stairs. There is ample space between tables inside. Seongsu is a place that mainly sells Korean food. This place is full of Korean menu items such as kimchi stew, garlic bossam, and green onion pancakes. There are many traditional alcoholic beverages such as makgeolli, ginseng liquor, and cheongju.

Side dishes include stir-fried fish cakes. I ordered a set for my friend. It comes with Seongsura kimchi stew and green onion kimchi and garlic bossam. Seongsura Euljiro Branch, a famous restaurant near Euljiro 3-ga Station, offers a variety of sets, including friend sets, couple sets, Beopka sets, and Sura sets. The kimchi in Kimchi Jjim is spicy and sour. The kimchi tears easily along the grain. Serve over warm rice. Kimchi jjim is also considered a rice thief. Pork boasts a soft texture. The kimchi garlic bossam comes in a generous amount. Bossam is surrounded by various ingredients such as kimchi and cabbage. The middle bell pepper has garlic citron flavored seasoning. I enjoy bossam in various combinations. Please note that Bossam only serves meat boiled on the same day. We make kimchi ourselves every day.

If you visit the Euljiro 3-ga Station restaurant Seongsura Euljiro branch for lunch, you can enjoy unlimited rice and makgeolli. I should come here and eat when I want to get drunk due to stress at work. Each menu has reasonable prices and good value for money. I especially recommend the set menu. Enjoy the perfect breakfast in Brisbane at 3Bro Kimbap!

When I stayed near King Street in Bowen Hills, I stumbled across 3Bro Gimbap, which was one of the highlights of the trip. This cozy Korean restaurant, a short walk from the hotel, provided a fresh, delicious, and hearty breakfast that was just what I was looking for.

I ordered light but filling tofu gimbap and warm soybean paste soup. The taste had the flavor of authentic Korean food, just like eating it at a kimbap restaurant in Seoul. The staff were friendly and the atmosphere was relaxed, making it the perfect place to start the morning leisurely before exploring Brisbane.

If you are staying nearby and looking for a special breakfast that is different from the usual cafe breakfast, I highly recommend 3Bro Gimbap. The price is affordable, the location is convenient, and it is a place where you can feel the Korean atmosphere in Brisbane.

reviews.author: 0IN YUN
reviews.text:
Octopus Bonga’s Haecheontang comes with a large chicken and a generous amount of various seafood such as octopus, abalone, and scallops.

When the octopus is cooked properly, it is cut into bite-size pieces and its texture is soft and chewy.
I tend to eat octopus a lot these days, and it was the biggest and most delicious octopus I've ever eaten.

The chicken was poached, clean, chewy and very delicious without any unpleasant smell.

In addition to the savory taste of the chicken and the cool taste of the octopus and seafood, the soup is slightly spicy due to the addition of sliced Cheongyang peppers, which cleanly cuts out the oily taste of the chicken, making the soup amazing.

Octopus Bonga was the best health food that was prepared with the freshest, best ingredients without using any techniques, allowing the natural taste of the ingredients to be felt.

reviews.author: Kevin Ko
reviews.text: This is a restaurant specializing in seafood such as octopus and octopus, located on the right as you go up toward Cheonggyecheon from Exit 3 of Euljiro 1-ga Station on Line 2. This restaurant was also aired on KBS’s Lively Information. Types of soup include Haewoo-tang, Haecheon-tang, Haesin-tang, and Octopus Yeonpo-tang. Haewoo stew contains beef feet and is really chewy and soft. The octopus was cooked well, so it was soft and delicious. The soup contains abalone, clams, mussels, etc. and the soup is refreshing and provides a soothing taste. Seafood is eaten dipped in vinegar sauce, and beef feet are eaten with soy sauce. The soy sauce sauce is unique and delicious. Some haewoo stews with beef feet contain octopus from the East Coast, while others contain octopus. It is said that Haecheon-tang contains chicken, and Haesin-tang contains octopus instead of octopus. It's not cheap, but it's great for a delicious soup and a glass of soju.

Usually, if octopus is added to seafood stew, it becomes Haesin-tang, if chicken is added to Haesin-tang, it becomes Haecheon-tang, and if beef feet are added to Hae-sin-tang, it becomes Hae-woo-tang. However, here, the seafood stew contains octopus instead of octopus.

If there are 4 people here, order the Haecheontang Sojja and add 2 servings of Kalguksu Sari and 1 serving of porridge, which is enough for a simple drink and meal.

The onban dish looks like a hot pot, or a beef stew, or something on the border between them, but the seasoning is strong as expected, and there are plenty of vegetables and ingredients, so the portion is generous.

The side dish was too sweet, whether it was cucumbers or pickles, the pickled radish seasoned with red pepper powder tasted like it was covered in salt, and the kimchi only smelled like bland Chinese cabbage.

It's disappointing. If you're going to hire foreigners who can't speak Korean properly, you have to be someone who can do the job properly, but they can't communicate and it's a mess...

In the past, I often ate frozen pork belly wrapped in tin foil, but recently I also enjoy salt-grilled beef.
However, the unit price tends to rise, and the salt grill is quite expensive, so if you eat to your heart's content, it can cost well over 50,000 won per person, so even though meat is meat, you can enjoy the atmosphere while eating side dishes and drinking to your heart's content.

reviews.author: SOLEILOS
reviews.text:
The number one menu item that comes to mind in chilly weather like these days is, of course, beef stew. I recently went to a famous beef soup restaurant that was popular by word of mouth, and it was such a satisfying meal that I thought, “Ah, this is the real deal” as soon as I took a spoonful.

When I first entered the store, I was impressed by the clean and organized atmosphere. It was easy to eat alone, and it was quite crowded with office workers during lunch hours. The menu centered around Yukgaejang and also had side dishes such as boiled pork and dumplings, but since it was my first visit, I ordered the basic Yukgaejang.

Yukgaejang, which came out a little later, received a passing grade from the looks of it. The generous amount of meat, green onions, and bean sprouts on top of the red soup was delicious. When I took a bite of the soup, I found that the deep, rich beef bone base and spiciness were just right, making it non-irritating yet addictive. In particular, the meat was soft and not tough, and the more you chewed it, the more the savory flavor came out.

The biggest advantage of this restaurant was the balance of the soup. It wasn't too spicy or too greasy, so I was able to eat it until the last spoonful without getting sick of it. If you roll it up with rice, the soup and meat go well together, making it the perfect meal. The kimchi and radish radish that came with it went well with the beef stew, further increasing overall satisfaction.

The price was reasonable considering today's prices, so it felt like it was cost-effective. The portion was generous, so it was good to eat well, and it tasted like it would be perfect as a hangover.

In general, if you are looking for authentic beef stew with a rich and deep broth, this is a restaurant worth visiting again. This is a place I would especially recommend to those who like spicy yet comforting beef stew.

Bean sprout radish soup, soybean paste, red pepper paste, green onion slices, kimchi, oil paste, garlic, sesame leaf lettuce wraps, Cheongyang pepper, etc. were served.
You can grill the frozen pork belly cut neatly and neatly on a grill lined with tin foil, and the foil is changed in between. It tastes even better if you grill it with green onion slices or kimchi. The meat is cut to the right size and thickness, so it has a good texture. Vegetables may be expensive these days, but they generously serve ssam (ssam).
I ordered fried rice by the time I finished eating all the meat, and they added the remaining meat, kimchi, green onion slices, red pepper paste, and ssamjang and stir-fried the rice and fried rice ingredients. The grill on the second floor has been changed to a round, translucent one (according to the employee, it has been modified).  The first floor appears to be a four-sided cast iron plate.
For some reason, the temperature seems to rise less due to the shallow grill.  It doesn't seem to taste like it's being fried in melted porcelain oil.  Of course, this will be a matter of individual taste.  They say the second floor is cool, but you should also think about your tastes.
The fried rice also seems to have a different degree of butter evaporation. The degree to which the rice is pressed is different compared to eating it from a cast iron plate. (I don't know if the cause is the grill). It doesn't taste like it was fried because it was cooked over a strong fire.
I can feel that they are kind and take an indifferent interest in making the place a pleasant experience every time.

reviews.author: Drive Thru
reviews.text:
★★★★★

The dumpling soup made with rich beef bone broth and the special fried dumplings are excellent!

I visited because I wanted some hot soup in chilly weather, and I had a really satisfying meal.

The dumpling soup has a really rich and deep flavor. Five large, filling dumplings are placed in a clean, flavor-free beef bone broth, and you will feel full after eating just one bowl. The combination of freshly made crunchy kimchi and kimchi is the best. (Kimchi can be conveniently brought from the self-service bar)

Be sure to try the fried Mansae! Crispy fried dumplings are topped with whole shrimp, which are truly delicious when dipped in the chili sauce that comes with them. It is great as a meal menu, and I think it would also be good to enjoy as a side dish with drinks with hotpot in the evening.

There are always a lot of customers during lunch hours, but the turnover rate is fast. Highly recommended if you are looking for a place to have a hearty and delicious meal near Jongno 3-ga Station.

Open after midnight

Food is coming too~

Above all, it was a nice place because they were friendly!

reviews.author: Kevin Ko
reviews.text:
Jongno 2-ga has been standing for a long time on Cheonggyecheon Stream.
This restaurant is famous for its country kalguksu (noodle soup).
The entrance to the restaurant is small, but the inside is quite spacious.
For lunch, I usually order and eat kalguksu (noodle soup).
In the evening, the store is filled with drinking customers.
The most popular side dish is raw cabbage bossam.

Crispy raw cabbage wrap topped with sweet and sour raw radish vegetables
It is very delicious when eaten with soft bossam.
Yukhoe has soft meat and a slightly spicy seasoning.
It was delicious mixed well with pears.

However, Bossam is soft but has a slight smell.
Raw radish vegetables and raw meat are delicious, but they have a strong sweet taste.
It would be much better if the sweetness was reduced a little.
Still, since it’s delicious, a lot of people will come here.

The origin of the food ingredients here is global.
Bossam is from Austria, fresh cabbage is from Korea,
Steamed pollack is from Russia, and stir-fried octopus is from China.

However, since the table is a sit-down table, if you sit for a long time,
The downside is that my back hurts.
It's a bit hectic because there are a lot of customers, but
The staff are generally friendly.
